newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures mixed, COB moves higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures mixed, COB moves higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed Monday, with strong buying interest pushing California Oregon Border (COB) contracts higher, industry sources said.
Despite the COB rise, sources said futures contracts were expected to ease this week following higher numbers through last week.
"We have seen one very large buyer out there (Monday), but I don't think the fundamentals are there for them to keep buying the market through the moon," said one Houston-based futures trader.
As of 1240 EST, May COB was up 25 cents at $11.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching as high as $11.90, while June COB was offered at $11.75 after trade in a range of $11.80-11.90 per MWh.
September COB had traded up 35 cents at $18.60 per MWh.
May Palo Verde (PV) was trading down five cents at $15.40 after reaching as high as $15.70, while June PV was down 14 cents at $16.40 after reaching as high as $16.70 per MWh.
September PV had traded up 26 cents at $22.60 per MWh.
Overall market fundamentals remained bearish, sources said, with generating capacity returning to service in the West and hydroelectric power expected to be plentiful in the late spring.

The 1,083 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon nuclear unit 2 in central California reached 50 percent power the weekend, while the 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 3 near Phoenix, Ariz., resumed full electricity production.
Although hydroelectric supply remained plentiful, the cooler-than-expected weather in the Northwest had slowed the rate of snowmelt and water runoffs from the higher elevations.
But sources said the delayed runoff would be more bullish for deferred contracts like May and June.
"It is not a question of how, but when (the runoff will boost hydropower)," the Houston source said.
As of 1215, NYMEX said an estimated total of 87 COB and 141 PV contracts had traded.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasts called for temperatures near normal along the coast through much of the week and four to eight degrees below normal in the east.
Some clouds and rain were called for on Tuesday, then conditions were expected to dry out on Wednesday with more shower activity across the north later in the week.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be near to slightly above normal Wednesday then dropping to below normal levels for Thursday, Friday and Saturday.
Along with the lower temperatures, skies were expected to be cloudy in the latter part of the week, with a chance of showers and upper elevation snows.
